title: Wiper-like activity
overview: Review an inert audit summary for mass deletion of protected resources outside a maintenance scope.
prerequisites: Know the basics of Linux auditing and how to review authorization context.

attack.name: Data Destruction
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: A mass-delete observation affecting protected resources without approved maintenance needs immediate integrity triage.
evidence: Review affected resource class, object count, writer and change record. Seek backup and storage audit confirmation.
false_positive: Retention enforcement or approved disposal can affect large datasets.
tuning: Verify lifecycle policies in advance and never suppress deletion on protected data solely because of volume.
response: Preserve storage logs, pause confirmed unauthorized activity and validate backup integrity before restoration.
prevention: Protect backups from the same identity plane and require review for large destructive changes.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The fixture comprises descriptive audit fields. No learner assets are deleted.

questions.explanation: Cache lifecycle operations can be high volume without the same impact.

options: Recovery depends on their integrity and isolation
questions.explanation: Shared access and untested backups can undermine restoration.
